item.title: US appeals court blocks Trump request to send National Guard to Chicago amid immigration protests
item.description: A US appeals court has blocked President Trump's order to deploy the National Guard in Chicago, citing a lack of evidence for rebellion or danger. The court found that protests against immigration policies, even if spirited, do not justify such a deployment. This ruling follows similar challenges from Illinois, Oregon, and California against the administration's use of federal troops domestically.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US shutdown: Deadlock to enter third week as Senate rejects stopgap funding bill for 10th time —Who to be blamed?
item.description: The US government shutdown persists as the Senate rejects the House's spending patch for the tenth time. Senate Majority Leader Thune is now proposing debates on full-year funding bills, hoping to break the deadlock. Democrats, however, insist on negotiations regarding healthcare, a key demand that remains unmet by Republicans.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Violated laws': ICE arrests Chicago police officer from Montenegro — Who is Radule Bojovic? Why is he in custody?
item.description: An illegal immigrant, Radule Bojovic, working as a police officer in Hanover Park, was arrested by ICE for overstaying his visa by over a decade. Officials expressed alarm at local departments hiring undocumented individuals and issuing them firearms, violating federal law and jeopardizing community safety. Bojovic, a native of Montenegro, had recently joined the police force.

item.title: 83-year-old McConnell falls in Capitol corridors amid ongoing health scrutiny — Watch
item.description: Senator Mitch McConnell briefly collapsed in the Capitol corridors on Thursday, requiring assistance from aides and a Capitol Police officer. This incident adds to recent concerns about the 83-year-old Republican's health, following several public episodes where he appeared to freeze while speaking.

item.title: Are fireworks banned in Dubai for Diwali 2025? What’s allowed, what’s not, and where you can actually celebrate
item.description: Dubai’s Diwali 2025 celebrations are set to light up the city like never before, blending rich cultural traditions with modern spectacle. Yet, beneath the vibrant festivities lies a strict framework governing fireworks and public conduct. Navigating these rules is key to enjoying a memorable, safe, and respectful Diwali in one of the world’s most diverse cities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Driven by fear’: Israel's Amichai Chikli slams Keir Starmer; gives stark message to UK — 'fight radical Islam or lose Britain'
item.description: Israel's diaspora minister, Amichai Chikli, criticized the UK Labour government's approach to extremism, likening it to pre-WWII appeasement. He claimed Prime Minister Keir Starmer fears Islamists and states like Turkey and Qatar, drawing parallels to Neville Chamberlain's appeasement of Nazis. Chikli warned this fear-driven strategy against a global Muslim Brotherhood movement could endanger Britain's way of life and liberties.

item.title: Afghan-Pak conflict: Taliban accuses Islamabad of drone strikes in Kabul
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban government accused Pakistan of drone strikes in Kabul, causing casualties, just as both nations declared a 48-hour ceasefire following deadly border clashes. Pakistan claims strikes targeted militant hideouts. The truce aims to halt bloodshed and facilitate dialogue, with Islamabad emphasizing Kabul's role in addressing demands regarding militant sanctuaries.

item.title: Who are the Talibros? Meet the content creators braving Afghanistan
item.description: A new wave of social media provocateurs, dubbed "Talibros," are marketing Taliban-controlled Afghanistan as an offbeat travel destination. These content creators repackage the country as a contrarian experience, downplaying human rights abuses and presenting a distorted reality to their audiences. Their content blurs the lines between shock humor and propaganda, exploiting distrust in traditional media.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'He threw away': Former US envoy slams Trump for straining ties with India, says president spoiled relationship because of ...
item.description: Former US envoy Rahm Emanuel claims Donald Trump damaged US-India relations due to ego and alleged financial dealings with Pakistan. Emanuel stated Trump "threw away 40 years of meticulous strategic planning" by straining ties with India, a key counterweight to China. This, he argued, has benefited China strategically and economically.

item.title: flydubai to provide free meals and in-flight entertainment on all economy fares starting November 1
item.description: Flydubai is enhancing its Economy Class experience by including complimentary meals and in-flight entertainment for all passengers starting November 2025. This significant upgrade, driven by customer feedback, will offer over 1,000 films, diverse TV shows, interactive games, and a variety of regional cuisine-inspired meals across its 135+ destinations.

item.title: Fire and ICE: How Chicago is resisting Donald Trump's onslaught
item.description: Immigration enforcement has shifted to Chicago's streets during Trump's second term, with ICE agents questioning residents and targeting sanctuary city policies. This aggressive operation, aimed at intimidating local officials, has sparked widespread resistance from residents and civil rights groups, testing the limits of federal power.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Arc de Trump’: Is US president building his own Arc de Triomphe in Washington, DC? — What we all need to know
item.description: US President Donald Trump has revealed ambitious plans for a new "Arch de Trump" opposite the Lincoln Memorial, inspired by Paris's Arc de Triomphe. This monumental project, intended to mark America's 250th anniversary, is part of his second-term agenda, which also includes White House renovations and other capital improvements. Trump envisions it as a grand gateway for visitors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'He knew I was 17...believed it was his birthright': Virginia Giuffre's posthumous memoir details Prince Andrew's exploits
item.description: ​When Andrew met Giuffre for the first time, Andrew was asked to guess Giuffre's age. "The Duke of York, who was then 41, guessed correctly: 17. 'My daughters are just a little younger than you,' he told me, explaining his accuracy. As usual, Maxwell was quick with a joke: 'I guess we will have to trade her in soon.'," says her memoir.
